correctness.rationale: The exact finite minmax recurrence has complete legal-move quantifiers and strict-mask growth. Two independent graph descriptions and reachable/all-mask algorithms agree on both initial values and each response class, for every first vertex; full all-mask evaluation of 16,384 and 262,144 possible masks makes the finite proof exhaustive. Vertex-transitive graph automorphisms justify opening-vertex uniformity. No extrapolation beyond the finite objects.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A generalized Petersen graph with 14 or 18 vertices contains a 7- or 9-cycle as its outer ring and is nonbipartite, while both subject graphs are bipartite; its exact table cannot apply. Ordinary-design domination cannot determine alternating minimax or exact second replies. Standard game inequalities impose constraints but are not equalities for arbitrary graphs.

originality.rationale: The three most direct primary works were inspected materially: the 2010 standard-game article proves general inequalities; the 2015 bluff study tabulates nonisomorphic generalized Petersen graphs; the 2014 design-incidence article treats ordinary domination, not game minimax. Seven semantic-record searches and targeted public searches found no equivalent numerical or two-ply geometric classification; results do not prove universal absence. The new full two-ply tables do not follow from the cited general bounds, ordinary domination, or generalized-Petersen table.
residual_risks: Semantic searches and inspected articles cannot exclude unindexed or unpublished equivalent numerical tables.

value.rationale: The two smallest canonical cubic finite-incidence designs provide an intrinsically motivated benchmark for adversarial domination-game play. Beyond known numerical bounds and ordinary dominating sets, the complete 2-ply tables reveal a sharp difference between universal optimal replies on Heawood and only two diameter-four replies on Pappus for Staller starts. This is a natural exact strategic classification of finite symmetric objects, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
